section_1.title: Introduction: The Archerfish Phenomenon
section_1.content: Hook the audience with an animation of an archerfish aiming at an insect above the water. Explain that the fish perceives the light bending at the air-water interface, introducing the need for a mathematical rule to predict this path.
section_1.example: An archerfish calculating the 'apparent' position of prey due to light refraction.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle of Least Time
section_2.content: Introduce Fermat’s Principle: Light travels between two points along the path that requires the least time. Connect this to the concept of velocity: v = c/n (where n is the refractive index).
section_2.example: Visualizing a lifeguard running on sand vs. swimming in water to reach a drowning swimmer in the shortest time.

section_3.title: Geometric Modeling
section_3.content: Present a coordinate plane with a boundary line. Define two points A (in medium 1) and B (in medium 2). Draw a path intersecting the boundary at point P. Label distances: x (horizontal distance), y1, y2 (vertical distances), and angles θ1, θ2 relative to the normal.
section_3.example: A split-screen animation showing the light ray path changing as point P shifts across the interface.

section_4.title: Mathematical Derivation
section_4.content: Express the total time function T(x) = sqrt(y1^2 + x^2)/v1 + sqrt(y2^2 + (D-x)^2)/v2. Set the derivative dT/dx = 0 to minimize time. Show the geometric steps resulting in sin(θ1)/v1 = sin(θ2)/v2.
section_4.example: Animated sliding equations where the derivative symbol d/dx simplifies to the ratio of the sines.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Snell’s Law
section_5.content: Substitute v = c/n into the result to reach n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2). Summarize that light bends to 'save time' because it moves slower in denser media.
section_5.example: Final diagram showing a laser beam passing through a glass block, highlighting the relationship between the incident angle and refractive indices.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0 # Centered towards right
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9 
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
